claims.text: The initial system is a zirconium-alloy cladding substrate coated with elemental Cr.
A continuous ZrN interlayer tens to a couple hundred nanometers thick is to be deposited between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
The deposited ZrN interlayer will form a robust diffusion barrier at the Cr/substrate interface.
ZrN has high thermal stability under the proposed service conditions.
ZrN is chemically compatible with the zirconium-alloy substrate.
The ZrN interlayer physically retards atomic diffusion between Cr and Zr.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion prevents interdiffusion-induced coating degradation.
Standard Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding undergo accelerated Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Elevated-temperature degradation of standard Cr coatings can lead to premature coating failure.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Approximately 300°C subcritical-water exposure represents normal PWR operation.
Steam exposure near 800°C represents an accident-relevant high-temperature condition.
The ZrN interlayer will remain effective during long-term water exposure near 300°C.
The ZrN interlayer will remain effective during short-term steam exposure up to about 800°C.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the ZrN-modified coating will exhibit substantially less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the ZrN-modified coating will exhibit improved adhesion.
The ZrN-modified coating will sustain oxidation and corrosion resistance in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction in interdiffusion, or obtaining comparable or worse mechanical or corrosion performance than the control, is designated as a falsifying outcome.
